props.title: Love Meetings

sections.content: Love Meetings represents Pier Paolo Pasolini's groundbreaking documentary exploration of Italian sexual attitudes during the economic boom. Shot guerrilla-style across Italy, Pasolini's probing interviews with everyday citizens revealed a nation caught between Catholic tradition and sexual revolution. The film's direct-cinema approach influenced later works like Husbands and Wives (1992) and When Harry Met Sally (1989), which incorporated documentary-style interviews about relationships. Pasolini's frank discussions of taboo topics like prostitution, homosexuality, and marriage set a new standard for cinematic investigations of sexuality.

sections.content: The film's influence extends into modern documentary approaches to sexuality and relationships. Deuce Bigalow: European Gigolo (2005) may have played it for laughs, but serious examinations like The Sessions (2012) and Interior. Leather Bar. (2013) follow Pasolini's lead in breaking down sexual taboos through frank discussion. Paris Is Burning (1990) particularly echoes Love Meetings' interest in marginalized sexual identities and subcultures. SUBHEAD: Documentary Innovation and Sexual Politics

Pasolini's interviewing technique - direct, unflinching, yet deeply empathetic - established a template for examining controversial subjects that influenced filmmakers for decades. Kinsey (2004) borrowed his approach for dramatizing sexual research, while documentaries like The Celluloid Closet (1995) and This Film Is Not Yet Rated (2006) continued his tradition of challenging cultural attitudes about sexuality through cinema.
